title: Timelines, Attributes, Marks, Signs & Conditionals
description: Five drops that move a decision out of JavaScript: constructed timelines, typed attr(), emphasis marks, sign()/abs(), and if().

drops.title: Timelines You Can Hold
drops.description: Scroll-driven animation with no animation CSS — ViewTimeline objects built in JS and handed to element.animate().
drops.concept: The CSS animation-timeline property gets all the attention, but ScrollTimeline and ViewTimeline are also plain JavaScript constructors. Building one gives you an object you can store, share across several animations on the same element, swap ranges on at runtime, and read currentTime off. Six cards each own a ViewTimeline; a document ScrollTimeline drives the progress meter and the hero glow.

interaction.mouse: Scroll the page — each card scrubs its own view timeline; the corner meter reads the document timeline.
interaction.click: Swap the animation range (entry / contain / cover / exit) and the lift, rotate and scale amounts.
interaction.touch: Same scroll behaviour; the control panel docks under the header on narrow screens.

drops.title: Layout Written in the Markup
drops.description: Typed attr() reads column spans, tints, radii, tilt and order straight out of HTML attributes — one rule, no inline styles.
drops.concept: The old attr() only worked inside content. The redesigned one takes a type — type(<integer>), type(<color>), type(<length>), type(<angle>) — and works in any property, with a fallback for when the attribute is missing or unparseable. A twelve-tile bento grid is styled by a single .tile rule; the control panel only ever rewrites attributes.
drops.source: OpenReplay · Using the CSS attr() Function for Smarter Styling

interaction.mouse: Drag radius, tilt and hue — every change is an attribute rewrite, not a style write.
interaction.click: Reshuffle the spans or reverse the order to watch the grid re-flow from the markup.
interaction.touch: The panel stacks above the grid and the bento drops to three columns.

drops.title: Marks Above the Line
drops.description: text-emphasis puts a mark on every character and grows the line box to fit it — stress that bold and italic can't express.
drops.concept: Emphasis marks (boten) are the East Asian answer to italics, and the browser reserves space for them rather than overlapping the glyphs. Three sub-properties cover shape, colour and logical position, and a quoted string replaces the built-in shapes entirely. The vertical sample shows why the position keywords are logical rather than physical.

interaction.mouse: Pick a shape, fill, position and colour and watch every sample re-mark itself.
interaction.click: Switch to a custom string mark and type your own character.
interaction.touch: All controls are native selects and inputs; the panel moves above the samples.

drops.title: Direction Without Branches
drops.description: JavaScript writes two signed numbers; sign() picks the side and abs() picks the amount, from one declaration.
drops.concept: Direction-aware hovers usually mean JS deciding left-or-right and toggling classes. CSS sign() collapses any number to -1, 0 or 1 and abs() strips the direction off the magnitude, so a single transform covers both directions, a centred bar grows either way, and a chip's arrow jumps to the far side — all from the same raw pointer delta.

interaction.mouse: Move over the tiles — they lean away (or toward) with no branching in the script.
interaction.click: Flip between recoil and attract, and dial the strength and radius.
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the tiles; pointer events feed the same two variables.

drops.title: One Rule, Every Variant
drops.description: Four looks times three sizes, normally twelve selectors, resolved inline by if() on two custom properties.
drops.concept: if() takes semicolon-separated condition:value arms and an optional else, and the conditions can be style(), media() or supports(). A button, an alert and a badge share one rule each; setting --variant and --size on their container re-resolves radius, padding, font-size, background, colour, border and shadow without touching a class.
drops.source: Marko Denic · Introduction to CSS if() and conditional logic

interaction.mouse: Pick a variant and a size — the components never change class.
interaction.click: Resize the window to watch the inline media() branch flip its own background and content.
interaction.touch: The state panel sits above the components on narrow screens.
